f.title: Reviewers decide from all the data whether a muscle injury signal is rhabdomyolysis
f.statement: There are no consensus criteria giving a specific CPK level required to diagnose rhabdomyolysis (commonly cited literature thresholds are a CPK elevation of at least five to ten times the upper limit of normal followed by a rapid decrease to normal levels with resolution of the inciting event; other cited thresholds are 1,000 or 5,000 U/L). If clinical reviewers observe a muscle injury signal, they will need to determine, based on their analysis of all of the data, whether to characterize the syndrome as rhabdomyolysis.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND Standard Safety Tables and Figures, Muscle Injury TAG v1.2): marketing applications with a potential muscle injury signal or muscle injury as an AESI; informative for applicants, not binding on them
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Rhabdomyolysis is considered a severe
manifestation of this type of injury, although there are no consensus criteria that provide
a specific creatine phosphokinase (CPK) level required for this diagnosis. Commonly
cited thresholds in the literature are a CPK elevation of at least five to ten times the
upper limit of normal that is followed by a rapid decrease in CPK to normal levels with
resolution of the inciting event. 2,3 Other thresholds that have been cited are CPK levels
of 1,000 or 5,000 U/L, although it is possible for patients to have levels above 100,000
U/L. 4 If clinical reviewers observe a muscle injury signal, they will need to determine
whether to characterize the syndrome as rhabdomyolysis based on their analysis of all
of the data.

f.title: Exclude CPK-only qualification when baseline CPK is elevated or CPK-MB exceeds 5% of total CPK
f.statement: Subjects with elevated CPK at baseline cannot qualify for the algorithm on laboratory CPK levels, to limit false positives from other underlying inflammatory muscle disorders. Subjects with CPK-MB above 5 percent of total CPK are also excluded, because a cardiac cause of the CPK elevation is likely.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice: subjects in clinical trial safety datasets analysed with the Muscle Injury algorithmic OCMQ; informative for applicants, not binding on them
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Subjects with elevated CPK levels at baseline are excluded
from qualifying for the algorithm based on laboratory CPK levels in order to minimize
false positive muscle injury diagnoses caused by other underlying muscle inflammatory
disorders. Similarly, subjects with CPK-MB levels greater than 5 percent of the total
CPK are excluded due to the likelihood of a cardiac cause for the CPK elevation.

f.title: Do not require rapid CPK resolution in the muscle injury algorithm
f.statement: Although the literature says CPK should rapidly return to near normal after the inciting event resolves (to exclude chronic muscle disorders), there is no standard definition of rapid resolution and clinical trial data do not routinely capture when the inciting event resolved; the algorithm therefore sets no requirement on how quickly CPK resolves.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice: subjects in clinical trial safety datasets analysed with the Muscle Injury algorithmic OCMQ; informative for applicants, not binding on them
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
References in the literature state that the CPK should rapidly return to near normal
values following resolution of the inciting event, but do not provide specific definitions for
what should constitute “rapid” or “near normal.” The intent of requiring rapid resolution is
to exclude chronic muscle disorders. However, given the absence of a standardized
definition in the literature for rapid resolution and the absence of routinely captured
information in the clinical trial data regarding the timing of inciting event resolution, no
requirement regarding the rapidity of CPK resolution was specified in the algorithm.

f.title: Qualify subjects for the muscle injury algorithm on any of four criteria
f.statement: A subject meets the Muscle Injury algorithmic OCMQ if any one of these applies: (1) any Muscle Injury OCMQ Narrow term; (2) urine myoglobin above ULN; (3) CPK above 5 x ULN, provided CPK-MB/CPK is not above 0.05 within 3 days and CPK was not above ULN at baseline; (4) the rhabdomyolysis triad reported as adverse events within 7 days: a muscle pain term and a muscle weakness term, plus either a urine myoglobin term or a dark-urine (chromaturia) term (the source names four specific MedDRA Preferred Terms; see quote).
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice: subjects in clinical trial safety datasets analysed with the Muscle Injury algorithmic OCMQ; informative for applicants, not binding on them
f.exceptions: The CPK criterion does not apply where CPK-MB/CPK > 0.05 within 3 days or CPK > ULN at baseline. Source inconsistency: Section 1.1 Background says the algorithm includes subjects with an AE of rhabdomyolysis or myoglobinuria, whereas Appendix 4.1 names only an AE of myoglobinuria in its prose and lists 'Any Muscle Injury OCMQ Narrow term' as criterion 1. Rely on the Appendix 4.1 criteria list and check the OCMQ file for which terms the Narrow scope holds.
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Therefore, subjects qualify for the algorithm if they meet any of the following criteria:
   1. Any Muscle Injury OCMQ Narrow term
   2. Urine myoglobin > ULN
   3. CPK >5x ULN and no (CPK-MB/CPK > 0.05 within 3 days or CPK > ULN at
      baseline)
   4. [PT myalgia + PT muscular weakness + (PT myoglobin urine present or PT
      chromaturia)] within 7 days
rows.review_note: Level Informative 2026-11-26 (Venkat chose option A, issue #634): FDA reviewer practice, not an applicant duty; FDA wording for its staff: Mandatory. Pass 3 double-check 2026-11-25: faithful; exceptions record the Background vs Appendix 4.1 mismatch; kept below 90 per SME.
